diagram.abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.title: [RTL] Diagram of the abdominal aorta with the renal and iliac arteries: normally the aorta below the renal arteries is on average 18–22 mm across; in an abdominal aortic aneurysm this segment usually widens all round to 3 cm or more, and a blood clot often lines its wall from inside
diagram.acute-limb-ischemia.title: [RTL] Diagram of the main artery of the leg, which divides into the lower leg arteries below the knee: normally blood flows through them to the foot and there is a pulse on the foot; in acute limb ischaemia an embolus is stuck where the artery branches, there is no blood flow below it, no pulse on the foot, and the foot is pale and cold
diagram.acute-rheumatic-fever.title: [RTL] Diagram of a section through the heart wall next to the mitral valve: endocardium, heart muscle and pericardium; normally the valve leaflet is thin and the layers of the pericardium lie close together; in acute rheumatic carditis the leaflet is swollen with nodules along its edge, there are foci of inflammation in the heart muscle and a thin layer of fluid in the pericardium; fused leaflets and valve narrowing are not shown
diagram.alcoholic-cardiomyopathy.title: [RTL] Diagram of the size of the left ventricle and how strongly it contracts, normally and in alcoholic cardiomyopathy: normally the ventricle is of usual size and contracts strongly; in the disease it is dilated and contracts weakly
diagram.aortic-dissection.title: [RTL] Diagram of the aorta cut lengthwise: normally the three-layer wall is intact and blood flows in one lumen; in aortic dissection blood passes through an intimal tear into the middle layer of the wall, and a flap of intima separates the true lumen from the false lumen
diagram.aortic-regurgitation.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left heart in diastole, while the left ventricle fills from the left atrium: normally the aortic valve leaflets are closed; in aortic regurgitation they do not close and blood flows back from the aorta into the left ventricle
diagram.aortic-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the aortic valve: normally, in aortic stenosis and after the valve is replaced with a prosthesis
diagram.aortopulmonary-window.title: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles, aorta and pulmonary artery, normally and with an isolated aortopulmonary window (type I, one of the variants): normally the aorta and pulmonary artery are separate vessels, each with its own valve, and the wall between them is intact; with the defect there is a window in this wall just above the valves, some blood from the aorta flows through it into the pulmonary artery, too much blood goes to the lungs, the pulmonary artery and left ventricle are dilated, while the valves stay separate and the ventricular septum is intact
diagram.arrhythmogenic-right-ventricular: [RTL] Diagram of the right and left ventricles in section and of the right ventricular wall tissue: normally the right ventricular wall is heart muscle whose cells are held together by desmosomes; in late-stage arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy the right ventricle is dilated, its wall is thinner, and in the outflow part, the inflow part and at the apex the muscle is replaced by fatty and fibrous tissue
diagram.athletes-heart.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart in section: in an untrained person the chambers and walls are of usual size and the pulse is normal; in a trained athlete all four chambers are slightly larger, the walls are slightly and evenly thicker and the pulse at rest is slower, which is an adaptation to training, not a disease
diagram.atrial-fibrillation.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse in the heart in normal sinus rhythm and in atrial fibrillation
diagram.atrial-flutter.title: [RTL] Diagram of the atria and ventricles: normally the impulse from the sinus node spreads over the atria and passes through the AV node to the ventricles; in typical atrial flutter the impulse runs in a large circle in the right atrium around the ring of the tricuspid valve, counterclockwise, through the isthmus between the inferior vena cava and the valve, and usually every second impulse reaches the ventricles
diagram.atrial-septal-defect.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart chambers: normal, with an atrial septal defect and after the defect is closed
diagram.atrioventricular-septal-defect.t: [RTL] Diagram of the four heart chambers normally and in the complete form of atrioventricular septal defect: normally the right and left halves of the heart are separate and blood flows from the atria into the ventricles through two separate valves, the tricuspid and the mitral; in the complete form there is one large defect in the centre of the heart directly above and below a common valve through which both atria connect with the ventricles, blood shunts from left to right at the atrial and the ventricular level, and all four chambers are enlarged
diagram.av-block.title: [RTL] Diagram of impulses travelling from the sinus node through the atria and the atrioventricular node to the ventricles: normally every impulse gets through; in second-degree atrioventricular block one impulse is blocked and the ventricles skip a beat
diagram.bicuspid-aortic-valve.title: [RTL] Diagram of the closed aortic valve seen from the aorta: normally the valve has three cusps that meet in the centre; a bicuspid aortic valve has two cusps, a smaller one and a larger one formed by two fused cusps, which carries a fusion line; the valve is not drawn narrowed
diagram.blood-flow.title: [RTL] Diagram of blood flow through the heart, lungs and body
diagram.brugada-syndrome.title: [RTL] ECG diagram of the right precordial leads V1 and V2: normally the ST segment after the QRS complex runs along the baseline; in the type 1 Brugada pattern the J point and the ST segment are raised, and the coved ST segment descends into an inverted T wave
diagram.bundle-branch-block.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse from the sinus node through the atria, the AV node and the bundle of His to the ventricles, with the ECG of one beat: normally the impulse travels down the right and left bundle branches, both ventricles are activated at the same time and the QRS complex is narrow; in right bundle branch block conduction along that branch is interrupted and the right ventricle is activated later; in left bundle branch block the left ventricle is activated later; with a block the QRS is wide
diagram.cancer-therapy-related-cardiac-d: [RTL] Long-axis diagram of the left ventricle before and after contraction: before cancer treatment all the walls contract well and the cavity becomes much smaller; with cardiotoxicity the same ventricle contracts more weakly, and a dashed outline shows how it contracted before treatment: doctors compare new results with this baseline
diagram.cardiac-amyloidosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart cut through all four chambers while the ventricles fill: normally the ventricular walls are of normal thickness and the valves and the septum between the atria are thin; in cardiac amyloidosis there are amyloid deposits in the walls; the walls of both ventricles, the valves and the septum between the atria are thickened, there is a little fluid in the pericardium and the left atrium is enlarged
diagram.cardiac-myxoma.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart cut through all four chambers while the ventricles fill: normally the mitral valve is open and blood flows freely from the left atrium into the left ventricle; with a myxoma a rounded lobular tumour hangs in the left atrium on a stalk attached to the interatrial septum, swings with the blood flow, drops into the opening of the mitral valve and obstructs blood flow into the left ventricle
diagram.cardiac-sarcoidosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of a four-chamber section of the heart with the conduction system: normally the impulse from the sinus node travels over the atria, through the atrioventricular node, the bundle of His and its branches to the ventricles; in cardiac sarcoidosis there are foci (granulomas) in the heart muscle (their places in the diagram are an example): in the interventricular septum at the bundle of His, where the impulse stops, and in the walls of the left and right ventricles
diagram.cardiac-tamponade.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart cut through all four chambers inside the pericardium while the ventricles fill: normally a thin layer of fluid lies between the layers of the pericardium and the chambers fill freely; in cardiac tamponade a layer of fluid or blood surrounds the heart, which is not enlarged, and presses on it, the right atrium and right ventricle are compressed, and all chambers are smaller because they fill less
diagram.cardiogenic-shock.title: [RTL] Diagram of a person with the heart, the aorta, the lungs and the organs: normally the heart pumps out enough blood and thick arrows carry it to the brain, the skin and the kidneys; in cardiogenic shock there is an infarct zone in the left ventricle, the heart pumps out too little blood, the arrows to the organs are thin, and confusion, cold clammy skin, little urine and congestion in the lungs are marked
diagram.carotid-artery-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the carotid artery in the neck and where it divides: normally the internal carotid artery, which carries blood to the brain, has a wide, smooth lumen; in carotid stenosis plaques at the bifurcation narrow the start of the internal carotid artery, and a fragment may break off a plaque and travel with the blood to the brain
diagram.catecholaminergic-polymorphic-ve: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse path from the sinus node through the atria and the AV node to the ventricles, with a ventricular cell close up: at rest the impulse takes its usual route, the rhythm is regular and the calcium stays in the cell's internal store; during exertion or emotion stress hormones reach the heart, the store leaks extra calcium and extra impulses start from several points in the ventricles, while the structure of the heart does not change
diagram.chagas-cardiomyopathy.title: [RTL] Diagram of a section of the heart with the conduction system: normally all chambers are of normal size and the impulse travels through the bundle of His, the right bundle branch and the fascicles of the left bundle branch; in Chagas cardiomyopathy all chambers are enlarged, there is an aneurysm at the apex of the left ventricle, and conduction is blocked in the right bundle branch and the left anterior fascicle
diagram.chronic-kidney-disease-and-heart: [RTL] Diagram of the heart and a kidney joined by an artery: normally blood from the heart reaches the kidney, and the kidney passes waste, extra salt, water and potassium out in the urine; in chronic kidney disease the kidneys filter less well, salt and water retention raises blood pressure and the risk of heart failure, blood potassium rises and increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders, the risk of atherosclerosis is higher, and heart and blood vessel disease in turn harms the kidneys
diagram.chronic-thromboembolic-pulmonary: [RTL] Diagram of the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery with its branches in the lung: normally all branches are open and the right ventricle is of normal size; in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension organised fibrotic material narrows some branches with a ring-like narrowing or a web and blocks one branch completely, less blood reaches the lung beyond it, the open branches are overfilled, and the right ventricle has a thickened wall and a dilated cavity
diagram.coarctation-of-the-aorta.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle, the aortic arch with its branches to the head and arms, and the descending aorta: normally, in coarctation of the aorta and after it is repaired. In coarctation there is a narrowing just past the left subclavian artery, high pressure above the narrowing, less blood flow below it and a thickened left ventricular wall; after repair blood flows freely down the aorta again
diagram.conduction-system.title: [RTL] Diagram of the conduction system: the impulse from the sinoatrial node to the Purkinje fibres
diagram.congenitally-corrected-transposi: [RTL] Diagram of the circulation, normally and in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries: normally the right atrium connects through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle and the left atrium through the mitral valve to the left ventricle; in corrected transposition the ventricles have swapped places together with their valves, yet venous blood still goes to the lungs and arterial blood to the body; the right ventricle pumps blood into the aorta, which lies in front and to the left, and blood often leaks back through the tricuspid valve into the left atrium
diagram.constrictive-pericarditis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart cut through all four chambers inside the pericardium while the ventricles fill: normally the pericardium is thin with a narrow cavity under it and the chambers fill freely; in constrictive pericarditis the pericardium is thick and stiff with patches of calcium and no wide layer of fluid under it, the atria are enlarged, and the ventricles are of normal size but fill less
diagram.cor-triatriatum.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left atrium and left ventricle while the ventricle fills: normally the left atrium is one chamber, the pulmonary veins drain into it and blood flows freely through the mitral valve into the left ventricle; in cor triatriatum a membrane divides the left atrium into an upper and a lower chamber, the pulmonary veins drain into the upper chamber, blood passes into the lower one through a narrow opening in the membrane, the pulmonary veins are not dilated, and the mitral valve in the diagram is unchanged
diagram.coronary-arteries.title: [RTL] Diagram of the coronary arteries, front view of the heart
diagram.coronary-artery-anomalies.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart from the front with the roots of the aorta and the pulmonary trunk and the coronary arteries: normally both coronary arteries start from the aorta and none from the pulmonary trunk; in anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary trunk (ALCAPA) the right coronary artery is wide and tortuous, blood from it reaches the left coronary artery through collaterals and flows back into the pulmonary trunk, and the anterior wall of the left ventricle gets too little blood and oxygen
diagram.coronary-heart-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of a coronary artery supplying the heart muscle: normal, and narrowed by plaques with one branch blocked by a blood clot
diagram.coronary-microvascular-dysfuncti: [RTL] Diagram in two halves: a large coronary artery on the surface of the heart and the small vessels it sends into the heart muscle; normally the small vessels widen with exercise and blood flows freely into the muscle; in angina with no obstructive coronary arteries the large artery is not narrowed by a plaque, and two mechanisms are shown: on the left, in microvascular angina, the small vessels do not widen with exercise; on the right, in vasospastic angina, a short segment of the large artery is narrowed for a while by a spasm; in both cases the muscle gets less blood
diagram.deep-vein-thrombosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of part of the lower leg with a deep vein in longitudinal section: normally blood flows up the vein towards the heart through open valves; in deep vein thrombosis a clot starts at a valve and grows up the vein, blood flow below it is slowed, the leg below the clot swells, and a piece of the clot can break off and travel to the lungs (pulmonary embolism)
diagram.diabetes-and-heart.title: [RTL] Diagram of a coronary artery cut lengthwise: normally the wall is smooth and blood flows freely; in diabetes plaques form in the wall and narrow the lumen
diagram.dilated-cardiomyopathy.title: [RTL] Diagram of the size of the left ventricle and how much it contracts, normally and in dilated cardiomyopathy
diagram.double-chambered-right-ventricle: [RTL] Diagram of the right ventricle, its outflow tract and the pulmonary trunk in systole: normally the right ventricle is one cavity with a thin wall, and blood flows evenly through the outflow tract and the open pulmonary valve; in double-chambered right ventricle, muscle bands in the middle of the cavity leave a narrow passage: below them is a high-pressure chamber with a thick wall, above them the outflow tract with low pressure and a thin wall, and the pulmonary valve in the diagram is drawn as normal
diagram.double-outlet-right-ventricle.ti: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles and the vessels leaving them, normally and in double outlet right ventricle (one of the variants, with the defect below the aorta and no narrowing on the way into the pulmonary artery): normally the pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle and the aorta leaves the left; in this condition both vessels leave the right ventricle, the left ventricle empties only through a ventricular septal defect, and mixed blood goes into both the aorta and the pulmonary artery, with too much blood going to the lungs
diagram.dyslipidemia.title: [RTL] Diagram of an artery cut lengthwise: normally LDL particles pass along the lumen with the blood; with high LDL cholesterol there are more of them, they are retained in the wall and form an early plaque
diagram.early-repolarization-syndrome.ti: [RTL] ECG complex diagram: normally the J point, where the QRS complex turns into the ST segment, lies on the baseline and the ST segment runs along it; in the early repolarisation pattern the J point is raised above the baseline and there is a notch at the end of the QRS complex, with the normal ST segment and T wave shown dashed; in a person without symptoms and without sudden deaths in the family this pattern is most often a harmless finding
diagram.ebstein-anomaly.title: [RTL] Diagram of the right heart: normally the tricuspid valve leaflets attach to the annulus between the right atrium and the right ventricle; in Ebstein anomaly the anterior leaflet is enlarged and sail-like, the septal leaflet is stuck to the septum and displaced towards the apex, the part of the ventricle between the annulus and the leaflets is atrialised, the functional ventricle is smaller, blood flows back through the valve, and the right atrium is drawn larger
diagram.eisenmenger-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles, the pulmonary artery, the aorta and small lung arteries in cross-section: normally the septum between the ventricles is intact, there is no shunt, and the walls of the small lung arteries are thin; in Eisenmenger syndrome there is a large defect in the septum, the pressure in the pulmonary artery is high, the walls of the small lung arteries are thickened, blood crosses the defect from right to left, and mixed blood enters the aorta
diagram.extrasystole.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse path from the sinus node through the atria to the ventricles, with an ECG strip: normally every beat starts in the sinus node and every QRS complex has a P wave before it; in a ventricular premature beat an extra impulse starts early in a focus in a ventricle, and on the ECG it is an early, wide QRS complex without a P wave, followed by a pause
diagram.fabry-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of a small area of the left ventricular wall seen close up, outer surface at the top and cavity at the bottom: normally the wall has its usual thickness and nothing builds up in the lysosomes of the muscle cells; in Fabry disease the wall is thicker, the muscle cells are larger, small deposits lie inside their lysosomes, and there are patches of fibrous tissue between the cells
diagram.familial-hypercholesterolemia.ti: [RTL] Diagram of a liver cell with blood above it: normally LDL receptors on the cell surface take up LDL particles and carry them into the cell, and there are few particles in the blood; in familial hypercholesterolaemia the receptors do not work or work less well, the cell takes up fewer particles, and many LDL particles stay in the blood
diagram.fibromuscular-dysplasia.title: [RTL] Diagram of a segment of an artery cut lengthwise: normally the lumen is even all along; in multifocal fibromuscular dysplasia narrowings alternate with widenings in the middle and far parts of the artery like a string of beads, and the initial part of the artery is usually unchanged; there is no plaque
diagram.focal-atrial-tachycardia.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse path from the atria through the AV node to the ventricles: normally the sinus node sets the rhythm; in focal atrial tachycardia a focus in an atrium fires fast, the wave spreads from it in all directions, and the ventricles usually beat fast and regularly
diagram.giant-cell-arteritis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the head from the side with the temporal artery and its enlarged cross-section: normally the artery wall is not thickened, the lumen is wide and blood flows freely to the scalp; in giant cell arteritis, in inflamed segments that alternate with unaffected ones, the wall is thickened, the lumen is narrowed and blood flow is reduced
diagram.heart-chambers.title: [RTL] Diagram of the four heart chambers in diastole and systole
diagram.heart-failure.title: [RTL] Diagram of how strongly the ventricles contract and how much blood they eject, normally and in heart failure
diagram.heart-valves.title: [RTL] Diagram of the four heart valves in diastole and systole
diagram.holter-monitor.title: [RTL] Diagram of Holter monitoring: a recorder worn on the body and the ECG recording
diagram.hypertension-in-pregnancy.title: [RTL] Diagram of a section through the uterine wall with the placenta lying on it: normally the spiral arteries in the wall are wide and plenty of the mother's blood reaches the placenta; in pre-eclampsia the spiral arteries are narrow and the placenta gets little blood, substances from the placenta damage the mother's blood vessels, her blood pressure rises, and her kidneys, liver and brain can be harmed
diagram.hypertension.title: [RTL] Diagram of an artery and the left ventricle with normal and high blood pressure
diagram.hypertensive-crisis.title: [RTL] Diagram of a person with the heart, the aorta and the target organs: normally blood pressure is in the usual range and the organs are not damaged; in a hypertensive crisis blood pressure rises sharply and acute damage to the brain, eyes, heart, aorta and kidneys is marked
diagram.hypertensive-heart-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left atrium and the left ventricle: normally the ventricle wall is of usual thickness, the atrium is of usual size and blood fills the ventricle easily; in hypertensive heart disease the ventricle wall is thickened all around and stiffer, the ventricle fills less easily and the left atrium is enlarged
diagram.hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy.titl: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle and its outflow into the aorta, normally and in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a thickened septum
[RTL] Diagram of the circulation, normally and in hypoplastic left heart syndrome: normally blood passes through the lungs and the body in turn; in the defect the mitral and aortic valves are closed, the left ventricle is small, the ascending aorta and the aortic arch are narrow, blood from the left atrium crosses an atrial communication into the right atrium and mixes there with venous blood, and the right ventricle pumps the mixed blood into the pulmonary artery and through a patent ductus arteriosus into the aorta and on to the body
diagram.hypothyroid-heart-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of the thyroid gland and the heart in the pericardium: normally the gland releases the usual amount of hormones, the heart beats at its usual rhythm and there is only a little fluid in the pericardial cavity; in hypothyroidism there is too little hormone, the pulse slows, and fluid may collect in the pericardium
[RTL] A schematic heart-rate curve over a day with a line at 100 beats per minute, and a heart with its sinus node: normally the rate at rest is below the line and goes above it only with exercise, then falls gradually; in inappropriate sinus tachycardia the rate is above the line already at rest and rises sharply with light exercise, the rises and falls are gradual, and the sinus node still sets the rhythm, as it does normally
diagram.infective-endocarditis.title: [RTL] Diagram of a heart valve: normal, and in infective endocarditis with a vegetation, a damaged leaflet, backflow and a fragment breaking off
diagram.interrupted-aortic-arch.title: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles, the aorta with its arch and branches, and the pulmonary artery, normally and with an interrupted aortic arch: normally the arch is continuous; with an interrupted arch (type B) the arch is broken between the left common carotid and the left subclavian artery, blood reaches the descending aorta and the left subclavian artery from the pulmonary artery through the patent ductus arteriosus, blood crosses a ventricular septal defect from the left ventricle to the right one, and too much blood goes to the lungs
diagram.intramural-hematoma.title: [RTL] Cross-section of the aorta: normally a wall of three layers, the intima, media and adventitia, surrounds one round lumen; in intramural haematoma, clotted blood collects in the media and thickens the wall in a crescent with no blood flow; no intimal tear or flap is seen, and the aortic lumen looks almost normal
diagram.kawasaki-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart from the front with the coronary arteries: normally the artery wall does not bulge anywhere; in Kawasaki disease a coronary artery aneurysm may form, a part where the wall bulges out and the artery widens; as an example, the aneurysm is shown on the right coronary artery

diagram.label.salt-water-retained-higher: [RTL] Salt and water retained: higher blood pressure, risk of heart failure
diagram.label.sinus-node-sets-rhythm: [RTL] The sinus node sets the rhythm
diagram.label.small-vessels-do-not-widen: [RTL] With exercise the small vessels do not widen
diagram.label.small-vessels-widen-with-e: [RTL] With exercise the small vessels widen
diagram.label.some-blood-shifts-to-leg-v: [RTL] Some blood shifts into the leg veins
diagram.label.spasm-narrowed-lumen: [RTL] Spasm: the lumen is sharply narrowed
diagram.label.spasm-narrows-artery-for-a: [RTL] The spasm narrows the artery for a while
diagram.label.string-of-beads: [RTL] “String of beads”: narrowings alternate with widenings
diagram.label.swollen-leaflet-nodules: [RTL] Swollen leaflet, nodules on its edge
diagram.label.to-abdomen-and-legs: [RTL] To the abdominal organs and legs
diagram.label.to-back-of-brain: [RTL] To the back of the brain
diagram.label.too-little-blood-to-brain: [RTL] Too little blood reaches the brain
diagram.label.tumour-releases-much-adren: [RTL] The tumour releases a lot of adrenaline and noradrenaline, often in surges
diagram.label.ventricles-sequential: [RTL] Ventricles activated one after the other
diagram.label.ventricles-simultaneous: [RTL] Ventricles activated at the same time
diagram.label.ventricles-swapped: [RTL] The ventricles have swapped places with their valves
diagram.label.vessels-do-not-narrow-enou: [RTL] Blood vessels do not narrow enough
diagram.label.wide-arteries-much-blood-t: [RTL] Wide arteries: plenty of blood reaches the placenta
diagram.left-ventricular-noncompaction.t: [RTL] Diagram of a long-axis section of the left ventricle, base at the top and apex at the bottom: normally the wall is dense (compact), and its inner surface is shown smooth as a simplification; in left ventricular noncompaction the outer compact layer is thin, and inside it lies a thick spongy layer of trabeculae with deep recesses that open into the cavity, most marked at the apex; the ventricle is the same size
diagram.lipoprotein-a.title: [RTL] Diagram of an artery cut lengthwise: LDL particles and a few lipoprotein(a) particles pass along the lumen with the blood; with high Lp(a) there are more of these particles, they are retained in the wall and a plaque may start to grow in it
diagram.loeys-dietz-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle and the thoracic aorta: the root, the ascending aorta, the arch with three branches and the descending thoracic aorta. Normally the aorta is not widened anywhere, and the arch branches are drawn straight for simplicity; in Loeys–Dietz syndrome the root and the ascending aorta are widened, and arterial tortuosity is shown, as an illustration, on the arch branches; after treatment the root and the whole ascending aorta are replaced with a graft of normal width, while the tortuous branches and the rest of the aorta stay as they were
diagram.long-qt-syndrome.title: [RTL] ECG diagram: normally the QT interval runs from the start of the QRS complex to the end of the T wave; in long QT syndrome the T wave ends later and the QT interval is longer; below, a normal rhythm and torsades de pointes ventricular tachycardia, with complexes that change around the baseline
diagram.marfan-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left heart and the aortic root while the left ventricle contracts: normally the mitral valve leaflets close; in Marfan syndrome the aortic root is widened, starting from the sinuses, and the mitral valve leaflets bulge back into the left atrium
diagram.mesenteric-ischemia.title: [RTL] Side view of the abdominal aorta with the three arteries of the intestine, the coeliac trunk and the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries: normally blood flows through them to the intestine; in acute mesenteric ischaemia a clot, which may come from the heart in atrial fibrillation, blocks the superior mesenteric artery and the intestine beyond it gets no blood; a separate label shows the chronic form, in which plaques narrow the arteries of the intestine
diagram.mitral-regurgitation.title: [RTL] Diagram of the mitral valve while the left ventricle contracts: closed normally, and in mitral regurgitation with a gap between the leaflets and blood flowing back into the left atrium, drawn larger as in severe regurgitation
diagram.mitral-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the mitral valve while the left ventricle fills (diastole): normally the leaflets open wide and blood flows freely from the left atrium into the ventricle; in rheumatic mitral stenosis the leaflets are thickened and fused into a funnel with a narrow opening, and the left atrium is enlarged
diagram.mitral-valve-prolapse.title: [RTL] Lengthwise diagram of the left heart while the left ventricle contracts: normally the mitral valve leaflets meet at the level of the valve annulus; in mitral valve prolapse the posterior leaflet is larger and bulges above the annulus line into the left atrium, and its chordae are longer and thinner; a dashed jet shows that the valve sometimes lets blood flow back into the atrium
diagram.myocardial-infarction.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle in longitudinal section and the artery that runs along its inferior wall: normally blood flows through the right coronary artery to the muscle of the inferior wall; in ST-elevation myocardial infarction a clot on a plaque closes the artery completely, blood goes no further, and the part of the inferior wall beyond the blockage dies through the full thickness of the wall
diagram.myocarditis.title: [RTL] Diagram of a cross-section of the left ventricle: a uniform wall normally, and patchy foci of inflammation in the wall in myocarditis
diagram.natriuretic-peptides.title: [RTL] Diagram: proBNP is cleaved into the active hormone BNP and the inactive fragment NT-proBNP
diagram.obesity-and-heart.title: [RTL] Diagram of the abdominal organs, three risk factors and the heart: normally there is no excess fat inside the abdomen, blood pressure, blood lipids and sugar metabolism are normal and the heart works without extra load; in obesity fat collects around the abdominal organs; this can raise blood pressure and disturb blood lipids and sugar metabolism, and the risk of heart disease rises
diagram.orthostatic-hypotension.title: [RTL] Diagram of a person who stands up, with a curve of blood pressure after standing: normally some blood shifts into the leg veins, the blood vessels narrow, the heart rate rises slightly, blood pressure dips briefly and holds, and the brain gets enough blood; in orthostatic hypotension the blood vessels do not narrow enough, more blood pools in the leg veins, blood pressure falls too far and stays lower, too little blood reaches the brain, and light-headedness and dizziness appear
diagram.partial-anomalous-pulmonary-veno: [RTL] Diagram of the circulation, normally and in partial anomalous pulmonary venous return: normally the four pulmonary veins carry blood from the lungs into the left atrium; in the defect (one variant is shown) the right upper pulmonary vein drains into the superior vena cava close to where it joins the right atrium, there is a sinus venosus defect high in the septum between the atria, blood passes through it from left to right, the right atrium and right ventricle are enlarged, and the other three pulmonary veins drain into the left atrium as usual
diagram.patent-ductus-arteriosus.title: [RTL] Diagram of the aorta and pulmonary artery: normally, with a patent ductus arteriosus and after it is closed. Normally the duct has closed and become the ligamentum arteriosum; when it stays open, blood flows through it from the aorta into the pulmonary artery; after it is closed, blood no longer flows through it
diagram.patent-foramen-ovale.title: [RTL] Diagram of the atria: normally the septum between the atria is whole, with the fossa ovalis on it; with a patent foramen ovale the two parts of the septum have not fused and overlap, with a narrow slanted slit between them through which a little blood may pass from the right atrium to the left on straining
diagram.pericardial-effusion.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart inside the pericardium: normally a thin layer of fluid lies between the inner and outer layers of the pericardium; with an effusion a wide layer of fluid surrounds the heart between the layers, while the heart itself is of normal size and not compressed; an arrow shows the distance between the layers, by which the size of the effusion is judged
diagram.pericarditis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart inside the pericardium: normal, and with inflamed pericardial layers and fluid between them
diagram.peripheral-artery-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of the main artery of the leg from the femoral artery through the popliteal artery and the lower leg arteries to the foot: normally the lumen is open and blood reaches the foot freely; in lower extremity peripheral artery disease a plaque narrows the femoral–popliteal segment, less blood passes below the narrowing, thin collateral vessels run around it, and the calf is marked as the place of pain on walking
diagram.pheochromocytoma.title: [RTL] Diagram of a kidney with its adrenal gland, the heart and an artery: normally the adrenal gland releases adrenaline as needed, the heart beats calmly and blood pressure is in the usual range; in phaeochromocytoma a tumour of the adrenal gland releases a lot of adrenaline and noradrenaline, often in surges, the heart beats faster and blood pressure is high
diagram.polyarteritis-nodosa.title: [RTL] Diagram of a medium-sized artery that branches and carries blood to an organ: normally the walls are smooth, all branches are open and blood reaches the whole organ; in polyarteritis nodosa inflamed segments with a thick wall and a narrow lumen are seen where the artery branches, on one branch small aneurysms alternate with narrowings, and another branch is closed by a blood clot, so the part of the organ beyond it dies (infarction)
diagram.popliteal-artery-aneurysm.title: [RTL] Side view of the leg: at the level of the knee the femoral artery continues as the popliteal artery, and below the knee blood flows through the lower leg arteries to the foot; in a popliteal artery aneurysm this segment of the artery at the knee is widened and pulsates, and a blood clot can form in the aneurysm
diagram.post-thrombotic-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of part of the leg with a deep vein in longitudinal section: normally the vein wall is thin and the valves let blood pass only upwards, towards the heart; in post-thrombotic syndrome the vein wall is thickened by scarring after the clot, the lumen is narrowed in places, the valves are damaged and blood flows back down the vein; pressure in the vein is raised and the ankle is swollen
diagram.postural-orthostatic-tachycardia: [RTL] Diagram of a person who has stood up: normally some blood shifts into the leg veins, the heart rate rises slightly, blood pressure holds and there are no symptoms; in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome more blood pools in the veins of the legs and belly, the heart rate rises markedly, blood pressure barely changes, and light-headedness and weakness appear
diagram.primary-aldosteronism.title: [RTL] Diagram of a kidney and its adrenal gland: normally the kidney releases renin, renin makes the adrenal gland release aldosterone, aldosterone makes the kidney keep sodium and water and remove potassium, and when there is enough fluid renin and aldosterone fall; in primary aldosteronism an adenoma of the adrenal gland makes aldosterone without a signal, renin is suppressed, blood pressure is higher, blood potassium is lower, and the heart suffers: atrial fibrillation and more damage than the blood pressure would explain
diagram.pulmonary-atresia-with-intact-ve: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles, pulmonary artery and aorta in a normal heart and in pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum (one variant): normally blood goes from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery and along its branches to the lungs, and from the left ventricle into the aorta; in the defect the outflow from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery is closed, the right ventricle is small, the septum between the ventricles is intact, and blood reaches the pulmonary artery from the aorta through the open arterial duct
diagram.pulmonary-atresia-with-ventricul: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles, pulmonary arteries and aorta, normally and in pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect (one of the variants): normally blood goes from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery and through its branches to the lungs, and from the left ventricle into the aorta; with the defect, the right ventricular outflow ends blindly, the pulmonary arteries are thin, there is a large septal defect under the aorta, the aorta is shifted and sits over it, the right ventricular wall is thickened, blood from both ventricles mixes and goes into the aorta, and from there reaches the pulmonary arteries through the open arterial duct and collateral vessels from the aorta
diagram.pulmonary-embolism.title: [RTL] Diagram of venous blood flowing from a leg vein through the right side of the heart into the pulmonary artery branches: normal, and in pulmonary embolism with a clot in a leg vein and an embolus blocking one branch
diagram.pulmonary-hypertension.title: [RTL] Diagram of the right ventricle, the pulmonary artery and small lung arteries in cross-section: normally the small arteries have a thin wall and a wide lumen, and the mean pulmonary artery pressure is 20 mmHg or less; in pulmonary arterial hypertension the walls of the small arteries are thickened, the lumen is narrowed, the mean pulmonary artery pressure is above 20 mmHg, and the right ventricle has a thickened wall and a dilated cavity
diagram.pulmonary-regurgitation.title: [RTL] Diagram of the right ventricle, the pulmonary valve and the pulmonary artery in diastole, while the right ventricle relaxes: normally the valve leaflets are closed and no blood returns to the ventricle; in pulmonary regurgitation the leaflets do not close, some blood flows back from the pulmonary artery into the right ventricle, and with severe long-standing regurgitation the ventricle dilates
diagram.pulmonary-valve-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the right ventricle, the pulmonary valve and the pulmonary trunk: normally the valve leaflets are thin and open wide, and blood flows freely from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery; in typical valvular stenosis the leaflets are fused into a dome with a narrow opening, blood passes through it as a fast turbulent jet, the right ventricular wall is thickened and the pulmonary trunk beyond the valve is dilated
diagram.raynaud-phenomenon.title: [RTL] Diagram of a finger and its small artery: between attacks the artery has its normal lumen and blood reaches the fingertip; during an attack of Raynaud phenomenon, brought on by cold or emotional stress, the artery is sharply narrowed by spasm, the fingertip turns white with a clear border, and the colour may change from pallor to cyanosis and redness
diagram.renal-artery-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the abdominal aorta with the renal arteries and kidneys: normally the lumen of both arteries is even and the kidneys are the same size; with stenosis an atherosclerotic plaque at the origin of one renal artery narrows it, the kidney beyond the narrowing is smaller and releases renin, and blood pressure rises; another cause is shown separately: fibromuscular dysplasia, in which narrowings of the artery alternate with widenings like a string of beads
diagram.restrictive-cardiomyopathy.title: [RTL] Diagram of the four heart chambers while the ventricles fill: normally the elastic ventricular walls stretch and the ventricles fill easily with blood from the atria; in restrictive cardiomyopathy the stiff walls hardly stretch, the ventricles of normal size fill less well, and both atria are enlarged
diagram.rheumatic-heart-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of the mitral valve seen from the left ventricle while it fills (diastole): normally the leaflets are thin, the commissures are free and the opening is wide; in rheumatic disease the leaflets are thickened, both commissures are fused and only a small oval opening remains; the heart chambers and blood flow are not shown
diagram.short-qt-syndrome.title: [RTL] ECG diagram: normally the QT interval runs from the start of the QRS complex to the end of the T wave; in short QT syndrome the T wave moves closer to QRS and ends earlier, so the QT interval is shorter; a dashed line shows where the normal T wave ends
diagram.sick-sinus-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of sinus node impulses travelling through the atria and the atrioventricular node to the ventricles: normally the sinus node fires regularly; in sick sinus syndrome two impulses in a row are missing and a pause follows; in the diagram neither the atria nor the ventricles are activated during the pause, and the beats from lower pacemakers that usually appear in a pause are not shown
diagram.single-ventricle.title: [RTL] Diagram of the circulation, normally and in single ventricle: normally the heart has four chambers and blood passes through the lungs and the body in turn; for the defect, one of its variants is shown, double-inlet left ventricle: both atria open into one large ventricle, the second ventricle remains a small outlet chamber joined to the main one by an opening, blood from the lungs and from the body mixes, and the mixed blood leaves into the pulmonary artery from the main ventricle and into the aorta from the outlet chamber
diagram.sleep-apnea-and-heart.title: [RTL] Diagram of a sleeping person's airway and heart: normally the throat stays open during sleep, air reaches the lungs and the heart beats at its usual rhythm; in obstructive sleep apnoea the throat collapses and no air gets through although the efforts to breathe in continue, the oxygen in the blood falls, the pause usually ends with a brief awakening, and the pulse may slow
diagram.smoking-and-heart.title: [RTL] Diagram of a coronary artery cut lengthwise: normally the inner lining of the wall is smooth and whole and blood flows freely; with smoking the inner lining is damaged, there is a plaque in the wall with a clot on it, and blood passes in a thin stream
diagram.spontaneous-coronary-artery-diss: [RTL] Diagram of a coronary artery cut across: normally the lumen is wide, lined by the intima, with the media deeper in the wall; in spontaneous dissection blood collects inside the wall (a haematoma, or false lumen) and compresses and narrows the true lumen; the narrowing is not caused by a plaque
diagram.subaortic-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle, its outflow and the aorta in systole: normally the outflow of the left ventricle below the aortic valve is free, the valve leaflets are open and blood flows evenly into the aorta; in subaortic stenosis a membrane with a narrow opening sits below an ordinary aortic valve, and blood passes through the opening as a fast jet
diagram.subclavian-artery-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the aortic arch, the subclavian and vertebral arteries: normally both vertebral arteries carry blood up to the brain and the subclavian arteries carry blood to the arms; in stenosis a plaque narrows the start of the left subclavian artery before the vertebral artery branches off, and when the left arm works, blood in the left vertebral artery flows down to the arm; blood pressure is lower in the left arm
diagram.superficial-thrombophlebitis.tit: [RTL] Diagram of part of the leg in longitudinal section: a superficial vein in the fat under the skin and a deep vein in the muscle; near the top the superficial vein joins the deep vein (the junction). Normally blood flows up both veins towards the heart. In superficial thrombophlebitis a segment of the superficial vein is blocked by a blood clot and the fat and skin around it are inflamed; the deep vein is not affected, and a dashed arrow shows the risk of the clot spreading through the junction into the deep vein
diagram.supravalvular-aortic-stenosis.ti: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta and coronary arteries in systole, normally and in supravalvular aortic stenosis: in the disease the aorta is pinched into an hourglass just above the valve, the valve is shown unchanged and open, the coronary arteries arise below the narrowing where the pressure is high, and the aorta above the narrowing is not widened
diagram.supraventricular-tachycardia.tit: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse path from the atria through the AV node to the ventricles: normally the impulse passes once, in one direction; in AV nodal re-entrant tachycardia an early impulse goes down the slow pathway, returns up the fast pathway and keeps circling, so the ventricles beat fast and regularly
diagram.takayasu-arteritis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the aortic arch and its three branches, front view: normally the origins of the branches are not narrowed and the pulse is normal in both arms; in Takayasu arteritis the wall of the aorta and of the branch origins is thickened, and the branch origins may narrow or close; as an example, the origin of the brachiocephalic trunk is shown narrowed and the origin of the left subclavian artery blocked, so less blood reaches the arms and the pulse in them is weak or absent
diagram.takotsubo-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle in a long-axis view, base at the top and apex at the bottom; the solid outline is the ventricle before contraction, the dashed one at the end of contraction: normally all walls, the apex included, contract evenly and the cavity shrinks along its whole length; in takotsubo syndrome the base contracts strongly and forms a narrow neck, while the apex and mid walls do not contract, so the cavity stays round at the bottom, like an octopus trap
diagram.tetralogy-of-fallot.title: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles, pulmonary artery and aorta, normally, in tetralogy of Fallot and after complete repair: in tetralogy, a ventricular septal defect, a narrowed right ventricular outflow tract, an aorta overriding the defect and a thickened right ventricular wall; after repair, the defect is closed with a patch, the right ventricular outflow is widened and blood may leak back from the pulmonary artery into the right ventricle
diagram.thoracic-aortic-aneurysm.title: [RTL] Diagram of the left ventricle and the thoracic aorta: the root, the ascending aorta, the arch with its branches and the descending thoracic aorta. Normally the aorta is not widened anywhere; in the example of a thoracic aortic aneurysm the tubular part of the ascending aorta above the root is widened, while the root and the rest of the aorta are of normal size
diagram.thoracic-outlet-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of the passage from the neck to the arm, front view: the nerves of the brachial plexus, the subclavian artery and the subclavian vein run to the arm past the collarbone, the first rib and the scalene muscles; in thoracic outlet syndrome the nerves (pain and tingling), the artery (the arm is pale and cool) or the vein (the arm swells and turns bluish) are compressed; all three sites of compression are shown together for clarity
diagram.thromboangiitis-obliterans.title: [RTL] Diagram of the arteries of the lower leg and foot down to the toes: normally the lumen is open and blood reaches the toes; in thromboangiitis obliterans the small and medium-sized arteries of the lower leg and foot have several short blocked segments with thin tortuous corkscrew collateral vessels around them, there are no plaques, little blood passes below the blocks, and the toes are cold and bluish
diagram.thyrotoxic-heart-disease.title: [RTL] Diagram of the thyroid gland and the heart: normally a gland of usual size releases the usual amount of hormones and the heart beats at its usual rhythm; in thyrotoxicosis the gland is enlarged and releases too much hormone, the heart beats faster, and the atria may go into fibrillation
diagram.total-anomalous-pulmonary-venous: [RTL] Diagram of the circulation, normally and in total anomalous pulmonary venous return: normally the four pulmonary veins carry blood from the lungs into the left atrium; in the defect (the supracardiac type is shown) the pulmonary veins join a confluence behind the heart, the blood rises through a vertical vein into the superior vena cava and reaches the right atrium, mixes there with oxygen-poor blood and passes into the left side of the heart only through the opening between the atria, and the right atrium and right ventricle are enlarged
diagram.transposition-of-the-great-arter: [RTL] Diagram of the circulation, normally and in transposition of the great arteries: normally blood passes through the lungs and the body in turn; in transposition the aorta arises from the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the left, so each circuit loops back on itself, and a little blood mixes through an atrial communication and a patent ductus arteriosus
diagram.tricuspid-regurgitation.title: [RTL] Diagram of the right heart while the right ventricle contracts: normally the tricuspid valve leaflets are closed and blood leaves the ventricle into the pulmonary artery; in tricuspid regurgitation the leaflets do not close, some blood flows back into the right atrium, and the atrium is drawn larger
diagram.tricuspid-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the right heart while the right ventricle fills (diastole): normally blood reaches the right atrium through the superior vena cava, the thin tricuspid valve leaflets open wide and blood flows freely into the right ventricle; in tricuspid stenosis the leaflets are thickened, the valve opening is narrow, the right atrium is enlarged, the superior vena cava is wider, pressure in the veins is higher, and the right ventricle is small
diagram.truncus-arteriosus.title: [RTL] Diagram of the ventricles and the vessels leaving them, normally and in truncus arteriosus (type I, one of the variants): normally the pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle and divides into two branches, and the aorta leaves the left ventricle, each vessel with its own valve; with the defect, a single common trunk with one valve leaves the heart above a ventricular septal defect, both ventricles pump blood into it, a pulmonary artery leaves the trunk and divides into two branches, and mixed blood goes both to the body and to the lungs, with too much blood going to the lungs
diagram.varicose-veins.title: [RTL] Diagram of part of the leg in longitudinal section: a superficial vein under the skin, a deep vein in the muscle and a short connecting vein between them. Normally the superficial vein is narrow, the cusps of its valves meet, and blood flows up it towards the heart and through the connecting vein into the deep vein. In varicose veins the superficial vein is widened and twisted, the cusps of its valves do not meet, and blood flows back down it (reflux); the deep vein is unchanged
[RTL] Diagram of a segment of an artery cut lengthwise: normally the wall is strong and intact and blood flows along the lumen; in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome the wall is fragile and can rupture even when the artery is not widened: the artery keeps its width, and blood escapes through a tear in the wall
diagram.vascular-rings.title: [RTL] Diagram of a cross-section of the chest at the level of the aortic arch with the trachea and oesophagus, normally and with a double aortic arch: normally a single aortic arch runs from the ascending to the descending aorta beside the trachea and oesophagus and does not encircle them; with a double aortic arch both arches persist, the right (usually larger) and the left, form a complete ring around the trachea and oesophagus and squeeze them from both sides
diagram.vasovagal-syncope.title: [RTL] Diagram of a standing person: normally blood pressure holds, the heart beats at its usual rhythm, blood returns through the leg veins to the heart, and the brain gets enough blood; in vasovagal syncope a trigger such as prolonged standing, pain or fear acts through the vagus nerve to widen the blood vessels and/or slow the heart rate, the leg veins are wider, blood pressure falls, less blood reaches the brain, and light-headedness and sometimes fainting follow
diagram.ventricular-fibrillation.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse in the heart: normally the impulse from the sinus node goes through the atria and the AV node and spreads through the ventricles as one wave, so they contract and pump blood out; in ventricular fibrillation many small chaotic waves run in many places of the ventricles at once, the ventricles only quiver, and no blood is pumped out
diagram.ventricular-septal-defect.title: [RTL] Diagram of the heart chambers: normal, with a ventricular septal defect and after the defect is closed
diagram.ventricular-tachycardia.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse path from the sinus node through the atria and the AV node to the ventricles: normally every beat starts in the sinus node; in ventricular tachycardia the impulse circles in the scar zone of the ventricular wall through a narrow isthmus, and every lap excites the ventricles again, so they beat fast and regularly on their own, apart from the atria
diagram.vertebral-artery-stenosis.title: [RTL] Diagram of the subclavian, vertebral and basilar arteries seen from the front: normally both vertebral arteries carry blood upwards and join inside the skull into the basilar artery, which supplies the back of the brain; in stenosis a plaque narrows the start of the left vertebral artery, past the narrowing blood still flows up it, but more weakly, and a fragment may break off the plaque and be carried to the brain
diagram.wpw-syndrome.title: [RTL] Diagram of the electrical impulse path from the sinus node through the atria to the ventricles, with the ECG of one beat: normally the impulse reaches the ventricles only through the AV node; in WPW syndrome an accessory pathway between an atrium and a ventricle conducts it earlier and excites part of the ventricle ahead of time, so on the ECG the PR interval is shorter, a delta wave appears at the start of the QRS complex and the QRS is wider

doctors.intro: [RTL] Heart Atlas is an open-source site about the heart and heart disease. Articles on diseases and tests cite clinical guidelines; the others cite reviews, textbooks and trusted references. No physician has reviewed the articles yet. We are looking for doctors who can help.
doctors.public: [RTL] Issues and pull requests on GitHub are public, and so is everything in the repository. You need a free GitHub account to write there. Do not send patient data, medical documents or copies of your diplomas. Your name goes into the article's public source file only if you agree.
doctors.review.text: [RTL] Read an article on the site, check it against its sources and send your comments. Once the article is corrected and you are satisfied, its page no longer says that no physician has reviewed it.
doctors.review.title: [RTL] Review an article
doctors.title: [RTL] For physicians
doctors.write.text: [RTL] Send plain text following the author template. No code or Git needed: we turn it into an article with diagrams and quiz questions and send it back to you before it is published.
doctors.write.title: [RTL] Write or extend an article

footer.disclaimer: [RTL] Heart Atlas is for learning and does not replace a doctor. If you have chest pain, severe shortness of breath or have fainted, call your local emergency number immediately (112 in the EU, 911 in the US and Canada, 999 in the UK).
